card.name: Patient condition before a risk statement
card.fires_on: Words inside a description of patients with a disease or pre-existing condition, just before the sentence says what they may be at risk for. Examples are diabetes mellitus, RA, pre-existing, underlying.

modes.label: Disease name after 'patients with'
modes.description: Part of a named disease in the group said to be at higher risk.
modes.example: Patients with type 2 diabetes mell<<itus>> may have fatty liver disease or cardiac disease

modes.label: Qualifier of existing illness
modes.description: Words like pre-existing, underlying or chronic that describe a prior condition.
modes.example: There is a potential for cardiac risk during sexual activity in patients with pre<<-existing>> cardiovascular disease.

modes.label: Verb or adjective linking group to risk
modes.description: A linking word right before the risk statement for a patient group.

card.plain: It marks the spot where a label names a group of patients with a certain illness, right before saying what risk they face.
